title: How Bluesky draws its logo on screenshots
titleZh: Bluesky 如何在屏幕截图上绘制其徽标
author: gavide
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Sometimes I take a screenshot of a post I like, either to send it to friends/meme channel or to save a “durable” copy. Like this one (I’ve cropped out the rest of the interface):
Original, if you want to reskeet it

I noticed the Bluesky logo in the right corner and thought that it was weird that the logo doesn’t bother me when I use the app. Then I looked at the post in the app again—logo wasn’t there, replaced by the “Follow” button. I remembered that a few apps hide their logo where the iPhone notch is, so that it doesn’t stick out, unless you take a screenshot. But here the logo is placed in the open, so how do they do it? I tried to take another screenshot, this time mid-switching to the other app:
The “Follow” button is visible when I take the screenshot mid-switch.

Did they somehow set up a listener for two buttons I’m pressing to take a screenshot and do a switcheroo at the last moment? I’m not an iOS developer, so I’m not sure what’s possible and what is not over there. At this point I was mildly intrigued. Thankfully, I remembered that Bluesky app is open source (or at least the code is available to look at). The answer was in the file literally called GrowthHack.tsx , introduced in January 2026 by mozzius. But it merely used a dependency, so to understand I looked into package expo-privacy-sensitive, also by them. The package creates UITextField with isSecureTextEntry property set to true and renders the actual content (the button) into that field’s .layer. When I take the screenshot, iOS hides this UITextField by blanking the layer, allowing the Bluesky logo to flutter its wings through (it was here the whooole time). For other platforms it simply renders content as-is, without masking. Why doesn’t it work when I switch between the apps? I suppose that iOS takes a snapshot itself at the start of the gesture (without triggering blanking), and when I do a screenshot, there is no live UITextField instance to react to that, only the inert snapshot. But once again, I’m not an iOS developer. Nifty trick or an abuse of API meant for privacy? The people in the thread adding the behavior mostly didn’t like it, before the thread got locked. I think it’s cute. I googled a bit, and the trick is well-known. Telegram implemented similar thing for its "secret" chats, as did Signal, so I don’t expect it to be patched by Apple any time soon.

comments.author: jjcm
comments.textRawHtml:
If it's between this and a perpetual logo, I'll take this any day.

I actually really like this approach. The action button isn't relevant in this context, and it doesn't occlude the content.

There's certainly situations where you wouldn't want this (ie if you're developing the app and you want to redesign starting from a screenshot), but for the average user I think this isn't overly hostile. I understand that people are dogmatically opposed to intent being modified, but I think you need to balance nuance. I actually enjoy having an attributable source in shared elements, and I think this is a low-impact way of achieving that.
comments.textZhHtml:
如果介于此和永久徽标之间，我随时都会选择此。

我实际上非常喜欢这种方法。操作按钮在这种情况下不相关，并且不会遮挡内容。

在某些情况下您肯定不希望这样做（即，如果您正在开发应用程序并且想要从屏幕截图开始重新设计），但对于普通用户来说，我认为这并不算太敌对。我知道人们教条地反对修改意图，但我认为你需要平衡细微差别。我实际上喜欢在共享元素中拥有可归因的来源，并且我认为这是实现这一目标的一种低影响方式。

children.author: blauditore
children.textRawHtml:
I actually hate that apps are allowed to blank out content on screenshots, and this can't be disabled. There are apps completely mis-using it, e.g. mobile payment apps which hardly show any sensitive data in most cases, but now I can't share e.g. infos on screen with someone else easily.

It's a classic case of someone discovering a feature and thinking "hell yeah, so much security" without understanding or caring about UX impications.

I've yet to see someone saying "oh, I'm so glad my screenshot was blacked-out because I didn't realize I was in a banking app". It feels patronizing.
children.textZhHtml:
我实际上讨厌允许应用程序删除屏幕截图上的内容，而且无法禁用此功能。有些应用程序完全误用了它，例如移动支付应用程序在大多数情况下几乎不显示任何敏感数据，但现在我无法共享例如很容易与其他人在屏幕上显示信息。

这是一个典型的案例，有人发现一项功能，然后想“天哪，太安全了”，而不理解或关心用户体验影响。

我还没有看到有人说“哦，我很高兴我的屏幕截图被涂黑了，因为我没有意识到我在使用银行应用程序”。给人一种居高临下的感觉。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
> I've yet to see someone saying "oh, I'm so glad my screenshot was blacked-out because I didn't realize I was in a banking app". It feels patronizing.

Yes, this. Payment apps, government apps, IM communications.

The other day I almost rooted my phone in anger trying to get around this, before pausing and realizing that this would only cause even more problems with those apps, thanks to remote attestation "features".

My favorite recent case, I almost locked myself out of mobile government services when changing phones recently[0], and it would've made for a stellar bug report showing when "fail safe" design can easily become "fail deadly"[1], with UI view of access and invalidation history clearly showing the timeline of a problem... if only I could take a screenshot of it. But I can't, because "much sekhurity".

--

[0] - Well, it's not really that big of a deal. With government services, there's always a way back. Might involve walking to a local civil affairs office or, worst case, a police station or a notary, but there is a way back. Big cloud services, on the other hand...

[1] - Invalidating a certificate prior to issuing a new one sounds like a good security idea, but in the real world fails critically if the two operations aren't an atomic group. In my case, issuing a new certificate failed, and I ended up walking around for half a day with old one invalidated and not even knowing it.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我还没有看到有人说“哦，我很高兴我的屏幕截图被涂黑了，因为我没有意识到我正在使用银行应用程序”。感觉很居高临下。

是的，这个。支付应用程序、政府应用程序、IM 通信。

前几天，我几乎愤怒地把手机扎根，试图解决这个问题，然后停下来，意识到这只会给这些应用程序带来更多问题，这要归功于远程认证“功能”。

我最近最喜欢的案例是，我最近在更换手机时差点将自己锁在移动政府服务之外[0]，这将成为一个出色的错误报告，显示“故障安全”设计何时可以轻松实现变得“致命失败”[1]，访问和失效历史记录的 UI 视图清楚地显示问题的时间线......如果我能截取它的屏幕截图就好了。但我不能，因为“太多安全性”。

--

[0] - 嗯，这并不是什么大不了的事。有了政府服务，总有回头路。可能需要步行去当地民政办公室，或者，最坏的情况下，去警察局或公证处，但还有回去的路。另一方面，大型云服务...

[1] - 在颁发新证书之前使证书失效听起来是一个很好的安全想法，但在现实世界中，如果两个操作不是原子组，则会严重失败。就我而言，颁发新证书失败，结果我逛了半天，旧证书失效了，我自己都不知道。

children.author: fluoridation
children.textRawHtml: On a similar note in terms of frustration, my bank ended up getting me to memorize my randomly-generated passwords twice because it blocked pasting. I guess it's to discourage writing them down in plaintext files, but I bet it just makes most people choose meaningful (and therefore weak and guessable) passwords.
children.textZhHtml: 同样令人沮丧的是，我的银行最终让我记住随机生成的密码两次，因为它阻止了粘贴。我想这是为了阻止将它们写在纯文本文件中，但我敢打赌这只会让大多数人选择有意义的（因此弱且可猜测的）密码。

Very frustrating.

非常令人沮丧。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
I once ran into a signup/login flow that allowed 36 characters in password when signing up but when logging in, the password field was limited to 20 characters.

I think I must have changed my password several times thinking I just copied it wrong or it had special characters that weren't allowed, but nope, the truth was somehow stupider than that.
children.textZhHtml:
我曾经遇到过一个注册/登录流程，注册时允许使用 36 个字符的密码，但登录时，密码字段限制为 20 个字符。

我想我一定多次更改了密码，以为我只是复制错误，或者密码中有不允许的特殊字符，但不，事实比这更愚蠢。

children.author: fluoridation
children.textRawHtml: I've seen that too. I was so mad when I finally figured it out.
children.textZhHtml: 我也看到了。当我终于弄清楚时，我非常生气。

children.author: garbagepatch
children.textRawHtml: Same here. Luckily you can show two apps at the same time in Android so I just put the password manager above the bank's app.
children.textZhHtml: 这里也一样。幸运的是，您可以在 Android 中同时显示两个应用程序，因此我只是将密码管理器放在银行应用程序的上方。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
Well, I did, after the fact, but it's only because I had a work phone on me (that doesn't yet actively block sharing to non-work devices).

I doubt most people have a second phone on hand, ready and able to capture actual screen shots when your phone is preventing screenhots.
children.textZhHtml:
嗯，事后我确实这么做了，但这只是因为我身上有一部工作手机（它还没有主动阻止与非工作设备共享）。

我怀疑大多数人手头都有第二部手机，准备好并能够在手机阻止屏幕截图时捕获实际的屏幕截图。

children.author: setopt
children.textRawHtml: There might be a market for a USB-C camera to take phone screen photos to immediately upload back into the phone.
children.textZhHtml: USB-C 摄像头拍摄手机屏幕照片并立即上传回手机可能有市场。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah, few moments ago it hit me there could be a market for a phone case with in-built camera(s) that photograph your screen at a shallow angle on demand, and transform that into a screenshot automatically.

However, my idea happens to hit a very new limitation: for some reason, "privacy filters" are suddenly a thing. New phones have them built-in as some new magic display function, and for everyone else, there's this mad marketing push to get people to buy and use privacy foils in place of glass/foil screen protectors.

IDK what's up with those. Since when "shoulder surfing" with smartphones is a real problem, and why do marketers and product designers bet there's so much latent demand for it?
children.textZhHtml:
是的，不久前我突然意识到，内置摄像头的手机壳可能会有市场，可以根据需要以浅角度拍摄屏幕，并自动将其转换为屏幕截图。

但是，我的想法碰巧遇到了一个非常新的限制：出于某种原因，“隐私过滤器”突然成为了一种事物。新手机将它们内置为一些新的神奇显示功能，而对于其他人来说，有这种疯狂的营销推动让人们购买和使用隐私箔来代替玻璃/箔屏幕保护膜。

不知道这些是怎么回事。从什么时候开始，智能手机“肩上冲浪”成为一个真正的问题，为什么营销人员和产品设计师认为它有如此大的潜在需求？

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
Recently handled someone's phone who had it. Neat technology. But the use case for it doesn't make sense, for the reason you specified.

The only thing I could think of is if you want to browse TikTok or Instagram in public and don't want people seeing the weird shit that's on your algorithm, but even then, that's kinda weird.
children.textZhHtml:
最近处理过某人的手机。整洁的技术。但由于您指定的原因，它的用例没有意义。

我唯一能想到的是，如果您想在公共场合浏览 TikTok 或 Instagram，并且不希望人们看到您算法上的奇怪内容，但即便如此，这也有点奇怪。
